sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien Language History. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics (PL 613). 298 pp.
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative work; Zao Min is sample language 11 (data via Wang & Mao 1995 / Mao 2004). No statement on Zao Min word stress. Sec. 2.1.3.2 (pp. 26-28): 'No language in the Hmongic branch has contrastive vowel length, nor do the Biao Min and Zao Min languages of the Mienic branch'; the only prosodic remark (p. 28) quotes Downer 1961:539 on Iu Mien reduced syllables with 'weaker stress and shorter duration.. strong iambic rhythm', explicitly about Mien, not Zao Min. Ch. 4 (p. 200): Zao Min keeps a regular /ʔa-/ noun prefix (citing Mao, Meng & Zheng 1982) and was called 'isolated' by Wong 1939:425…
